newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude interest seen amid closed arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude interest seen amid closed arb.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude interest was seen amid a tightly shut arbitrage, but activity was light due to prohibitive cost of highly-sought distillate crudes.
"The arbitrage is completely shut now, even if a VLCC is used for freight economics," an East Coast trader said, noting strong demand in Europe for light crudes.
Brent was barely discussed in the U.S. with only moderate speculation that a Wall Street trader collecting several Brent stems would probably bypass the U.S. market.
As a result of tight foreign light grades, local Louisiana sweet grades gained more support.
U.S. Gulf heavy sours received comparatively less interest in the Gulf Coast where supplies were balanced and domestic grades proved good alternatives, traders said.
Oriente crude was rumored sold Thursday at West Texas Intermediate minus $2.65 cif for mid Nov, but the low price could not be immediately verified.
In nearby markets, Argentine YPF was seen offering a Nov 23-24 Escalante at Dec WTI minus $3.05 fob.
Brazil's state Petrobras bought a parcel at WTI -$3.12 fob for Nov 16-17 on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Ecopetrol inquired about buying interest for another three cargoes of South Blend crude for November through January.
In the U.S. after market, outright Brent for Dec traded higher than the London session at $23.65 for partials, with full boats traded at $23.69 and $23.70 a barrel.
Intermonth Nov/Dec Brent changed hands at 35 cents, within the range seen in late London.
